messages.content: When registering a high-risk AI system in the EU database under the EU AI Act, what specific information must the provider submit? List the required items.

0.answer: Before placing a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III on the market or putting it into service, the provider or, where applicable, the authorised representative must register themselves and the system in the EU database maintained by the Commission under Article 71, entering the data listed in Section A of Annex VIII. Those items are the provider's name, address and contact details, the same details for any person submitting on the provider's behalf, the same details for the authorised representative where applicable, the AI system trade name and any additional unambiguous reference allowing identification and traceability, a description of the intended purpose and of the components and functions supported, a basic and concise description of the information used by the system (data, inputs) and its operating logic, the status of the system (on the market or in service, no longer placed on the market or in service, recalled), the type, number and expiry date of the certificate issued by the notified body with that body's name or identification number where applicable, a scanned copy of that certificate where applicable, the Member States in which the system has been placed on the market, put into service or made available, a copy of the EU declaration of conformity drawn up under Article 47, electronic instructions for use, and an optional URL for additional information. Electronic instructions for use are not submitted for high-risk AI systems in the areas of law enforcement or migration, asylum and border control management referred to in Annex III, points 1, 6 and 7, and for those systems the registration is made in a secure non-public section of the database limited to Annex VIII Section A, points 1 to 10, excluding points 6, 8 and 9. High-risk AI systems in point 2 of Annex III are registered at national level rather than in the EU database under Article 49.

1.answer: Before placing a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III on the market or putting it into service, the provider (or, where applicable, the authorised representative) registers itself and the system in the EU database, entering the data of Section A of Annex VIII (Article 49(1); Article 71(2)). Section A requires: the name, address and contact details of the provider; where another person submits the information on the provider's behalf, that person's name, address and contact details; the name, address and contact details of the authorised representative, where applicable; the AI system trade name and any additional unambiguous reference allowing identification and traceability of the system; a description of the intended purpose of the AI system and of the components and functions supported through it; a basic and concise description of the information used by the system (data, inputs) and its operating logic; the status of the AI system (on the market, or in service; no longer placed on the market/in service, recalled); the type, number and expiry date of the certificate issued by the notified body and that body's name or identification number, where applicable; a scanned copy of that certificate, where applicable; any Member States in which the system has been placed on the market, put into service or made available in the Union; a copy of the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47; electronic instructions for use; and, optionally, a URL for additional information (Annex VIII, Section A). The information must thereafter be kept up to date (Annex VIII, Section A). For systems in the areas of law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management (Annex III, points 1, 6 and 7), electronic instructions for use are not provided (Annex VIII, Section A), and registration takes place in a secure non-public section of the database limited to Section A, points 1 to 10, excluding points 6, 8 and 9 (Article 49(4)). Where the provider has concluded under Article 6(3) that its Annex III system is not high-risk, registration is instead under Article 49(2) with the Section B data (Article 71(2)); high-risk systems referred to in point 2 of Annex III are registered at national level rather than in the EU database (Article 49(5)).

messages.content: Under Article 10(5) of the EU AI Act, when may a provider of a high-risk AI system process special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction, and what key safeguards/conditions must be met?

1.answer: Under Article 10(5), a provider of a high-risk AI system may exceptionally process special categories of personal data only to the extent strictly necessary to ensure bias detection and correction, subject to appropriate safeguards. Article 10(5) requires all of the following: the bias work cannot be done with other data, including synthetic or anonymised data (a); technical limits on re-use plus state-of-the-art security and pseudonymisation (b); strict, documented access controls to prevent misuse (c); no transmission or transfer to other parties (d); deletion once the bias is corrected or the retention period ends, whichever is first (e); and records of processing documenting why it was strictly necessary (f).

0.answer: Under Article 10(5), a provider of a high-risk AI system may exceptionally process special categories of personal data only to the extent strictly necessary to ensure bias detection and correction, subject to appropriate safeguards. Article 10(5) requires all of the following: the bias work cannot be done with other data, including synthetic or anonymised data (a); technical limits on re-use plus state-of-the-art security and pseudonymisation (b); strict, documented access controls to prevent misuse (c); no transmission or transfer to other parties (d); deletion once the bias is corrected or the retention period ends, whichever is first (e); and records of processing documenting why it was strictly necessary (f).

messages.content: Under the EU AI Act, what minimum elements must a provider's quality management system (QMS) for high-risk AI systems include? List the required elements.

0.answer: A provider of a high-risk AI system must put in place a quality management system that ensures compliance with the Regulation and is documented in a systematic and orderly manner as written policies, procedures and instructions, comprising at least thirteen aspects under Article 17(1). Those are a strategy for regulatory compliance including conformity assessment and management of modifications, techniques for design, design control and design verification, techniques for development, quality control and quality assurance, examination, test and validation procedures before, during and after development together with their frequency, technical specifications and standards to be applied plus the means used where harmonised standards are not applied in full, systems and procedures for data management covering acquisition, collection, analysis, labelling, storage, filtration, mining, aggregation and retention, the risk management system referred to in Article 9, the setting-up, implementation and maintenance of a post-market monitoring system in accordance with Article 72, procedures for reporting a serious incident in accordance with Article 73, handling of communication with national competent authorities, other relevant authorities, notified bodies, other operators, customers and other interested parties, systems and procedures for record-keeping of all relevant documentation and information, resource management including security-of-supply measures, and an accountability framework setting out the responsibilities of management and other staff for all those aspects. Implementation of these aspects is proportionate to the size of the provider's organisation, while the provider must in any event respect the degree of rigour and level of protection needed for compliance (Article 17(2)). Providers already subject to quality management obligations or an equivalent function under sectoral Union law may integrate these aspects into that system (Article 17(3)), and financial institutions subject to internal governance requirements under Union financial services law are deemed to fulfil the obligation by complying with those rules, except for the risk management system, post-market monitoring and serious incident reporting aspects (Article 17(4)).

1.answer: Under Article 17(1), providers of high-risk AI systems must put in place a quality management system ensuring compliance with the Regulation, documented in a systematic and orderly manner in the form of written policies, procedures and instructions, and covering at least thirteen aspects: (a) a strategy for regulatory compliance, including compliance with conformity assessment procedures and procedures for the management of modifications to the system; (b) techniques, procedures and systematic actions for design, design control and design verification; (c) techniques, procedures and systematic actions for development, quality control and quality assurance; (d) examination, test and validation procedures to be carried out before, during and after development, and the frequency with which they are carried out; (e) technical specifications, including standards, to be applied and, where harmonised standards are not applied in full or do not cover all relevant Chapter III, Section 2 requirements, the means used to ensure compliance with those requirements; (f) systems and procedures for data management, including acquisition, collection, analysis, labelling, storage, filtration, mining, aggregation and retention, and any other data operation performed before and for the purpose of placing on the market or putting into service; (g) the risk management system referred to in Article 9; (h) the setting-up, implementation and maintenance of a post-market monitoring system in accordance with Article 72; (i) procedures related to the reporting of a serious incident in accordance with Article 73; (j) the handling of communication with national competent authorities, other relevant authorities including those providing or supporting access to data, notified bodies, other operators, customers or other interested parties; (k) systems and procedures for record-keeping of all relevant documentation and information; (l) resource management, including security-of-supply related measures; and (m) an accountability framework setting out the responsibilities of management and other staff for all those aspects. Implementation of these aspects is proportionate to the size of the provider's organisation, while the provider must in any event respect the degree of rigour and level of protection required for compliance (Article 17(2)). Providers already subject to quality management obligations or an equivalent function under sectoral Union law may integrate these aspects into that system (Article 17(3)), and providers that are financial institutions subject to internal governance requirements under Union financial services law are deemed to fulfil the obligation by complying with those rules, except as regards points (g), (h) and (i) (Article 17(4)).

messages.content: Under the EU AI Act, what is the scientific panel of independent experts, what are its main support/advisory tasks, and what key characteristics/selection requirements apply to its members?

1.answer: The scientific panel is a panel of independent experts that the Commission establishes by implementing act, adopted under the examination procedure of Article 98(2), to support the enforcement activities under the Regulation; the Commission, in consultation with the Board, determines the number of experts according to the needs and ensures fair gender and geographical representation (Article 68(1) and (2)). Its role is to advise and support the AI Office, in particular by: supporting implementation and enforcement of the Regulation as regards general-purpose AI models and systems, alerting the AI Office of possible systemic risks at Union level of general-purpose AI models in accordance with Article 90, contributing to the development of tools and methodologies for evaluating the capabilities of general-purpose AI models and systems, including through benchmarks, advising on the classification of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, advising on the classification of various general-purpose AI models and systems, and contributing to the development of tools and templates; supporting the work of market surveillance authorities at their request; supporting cross-border market surveillance activities as referred to in Article 74(11), without prejudice to the powers of market surveillance authorities; and supporting the AI Office in carrying out its duties in the context of the Union safeguard procedure pursuant to Article 81 (Article 68(3)). Members are selected by the Commission on the basis of up-to-date scientific or technical expertise in the field of AI necessary for those tasks, and must demonstrate all of the following: particular expertise and competence and scientific or technical expertise in the field of AI; independence from any provider of AI systems or general-purpose AI models; and an ability to carry out activities diligently, accurately and objectively (Article 68(2)). In performing their tasks, the experts must act with impartiality and objectivity, ensure the confidentiality of information and data obtained, and neither seek nor take instructions from anyone when exercising their Article 68(3) tasks; each expert must draw up a publicly available declaration of interests, and the AI Office must establish systems and procedures to actively manage and prevent potential conflicts of interest (Article 68(4)). The implementing act also lays down the conditions, procedures and detailed arrangements for the panel and its members to issue alerts and to request the assistance of the AI Office (Article 68(5)).

0.answer: The scientific panel is a body of independent experts established by Commission implementing act under Article 68 to support the enforcement activities under the Regulation, in particular the enforcement of the general-purpose AI model rules. Its support tasks are to alert the AI Office to possible systemic risks at Union level of general-purpose AI models in accordance with Article 90, which allows the panel to issue a qualified alert where it suspects a model poses a concrete identifiable risk at Union level, to contribute to the development of tools and methodologies for evaluating capabilities of general-purpose AI models and systems including through benchmarks, to advise on the classification of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, to advise on the classification of various general-purpose AI models and systems, and to contribute to the development of tools and templates. Members must perform their tasks with impartiality and objectivity, ensure the confidentiality of information and data obtained, and neither seek nor take instructions from anyone when exercising those tasks, and each expert must draw up a publicly available declaration of interests, with the AI Office operating systems and procedures to actively manage and prevent potential conflicts of interest. The same implementing act, adopted under the examination procedure of Article 98(2), lays down the conditions, procedures and detailed arrangements for the panel and its members to issue alerts and to request the assistance of the AI Office.
